answer.rationale: With only one experiment slot, the objective is sustainable qualified revenue, not just short-term trial volume. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but it targets small, price-sensitive accounts and only has a 12-week record of revenue/trial lift without evidence on retention or account quality — matching a competitor's discount race risks attracting low-LTV customers and eroding margins, a downstream value risk worth flagging rather than acting on immediately. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and two independent prior memories (31, 86) both attribute activation and adoption gains to onboarding simplification, giving convergent evidence and a plausible causal link to the current onboarding and activation declines simultaneously. I verify both onboarding memories before committing since they underpin the one experiment I can run this week, checking for consistency, sample size, and whether effects were durable rather than novelty-driven. Activation messaging (memory_91) and enterprise sales assist (memory_44) are reasonable alternatives but address only one of the two current regressions or a segment not under acute pressure. Referral incentives target retained customers, not the urgent SMB/activation issues at hand. I'm running this as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout to preserve optionality and re-test given the current environment differs from when the original onboarding findings were consolidated.
